The '''classical Lie algebras''' are finite-dimensional [[Lie algebra]]s over a field which can be classified into four types <math> A_n </math>, <math> B_n </math>, <math> C_n </math> and <math> D_n </math>, where for <math>\mathfrak{gl}(n)</math> the [[General linear group|general linear Lie algebra]] and <math> I_n  </math> the <math> n \times n  </math> [[identity matrix]]:

* <math> A_n := \mathfrak{sl}(n+1) = \{ x \in \mathfrak{gl}(n+1) : \text{tr}(x) = 0 \} </math>, the ''special linear Lie algebra'';
* <math> B_n := \mathfrak{o}(2n+1) = \{ x \in \mathfrak{gl}(2n+1) : x + x^{T} = 0 \} </math>, the ''odd orthogonal Lie algebra'';
* <math> C_n := \mathfrak{sp}(2n) = \{ x \in \mathfrak{gl}(2n) : J_nx + x^{T}J_n = 0, J_n = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & I_n \\ -I_n & 0 \end{pmatrix} \}  </math>, the ''symplectic Lie algebra''; and
* <math> D_n := \mathfrak{o}(2n) = \{ x \in \mathfrak{gl}(2n) : x + x^{T} = 0 \}  </math>, the ''even orthogonal Lie algebra''.

Except for the low-dimensional cases <math> D_1 = \mathfrak{so}(2) </math> and <math> D_2 = \mathfrak{so}(4) </math>, the classical Lie algebras are [[Simple Lie algebra|simple]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Dictionary on Lie algebras and superalgebras|last1=Antonino|first1=Sciarrino|last2=Paul|first2=Sorba|date=2000-01-01|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=9780122653407|oclc=468609320}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Sthanumoorthy|first=Neelacanta|title=Introduction to finite and infinite dimensional lie (super)algebras|date=18 April 2016|publisher=Amsterdam Elsevie|isbn=9780128046753|location=|pages=|oclc=952065417}}</ref>

The [[Moyal bracket|Moyal algebra]] is an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra that contains all classical Lie algebras as subalgebras.
